clue.text: It's rather pawsh means of revealing the government's intentions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the monarch's way of talking, spelt pawsh to mimic a cut-glass royal accent

definitions.text: means of revealing the government's intentions
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the address read at the State Opening of Parliament setting out the government's programme

explanation.walkthrough: The spelling pawsh imitates a plummy vowel, so the first half asks for how Her Majesty talks; the second half is the formal speech from the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's address opening each parliamentary session is written by ministers to announce their planned legislation, and her accent is famously plummy.

clue.text: The bloke'll peak before a year, with terrible consequences

indicators.note: he'll comes before the rest

parts.note: the bloke will is he will, contracted to he'll
the top is the peak
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man reaches his peak before the year is out, and it ends badly.
explanation.definitionFit: There will be hell to pay is an idiom warning of serious trouble or punishment to come.

clue.text: Soundbite Queen, second to suck off toe

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word suck

parts.note: the word whose second letter is used

indicators.note: off says the letters of toe are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about the Queen and a royal sucking toes, recalling Fergie's scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1992 toe-sucking photos of the Duchess of York are the joke behind the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundbite is a short memorable extract repeated in the media, which is a quotation.

clue.text: Old German prince preferred love with scrubber finally

parts.note: to elect is to choose, so the preferred one is elect
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: finally gives the last letter of scrubber

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used

explanation.surface: A noble from the old German lands chose to love a cleaner, or a tart.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubber is also British slang for a promiscuous woman, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electors were princes of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to vote for the Emperor.

clue.text: Corner that is for coy sex

parts.note: a nook is a corner or recess

explanation.surface: A quiet corner, that is, for a bashful bit of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is a playful, euphemistic British word for sexual intercourse, used to avoid naming it directly.

clue.text: National player takes Mermaid's lead, playing the Queen

indicators.note: the cap takes in a letter, holding it inside itself

parts.note: a player picked for the national side wins a cap, so is himself a cap

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: An international footballer appears at the Mermaid Theatre, cast as Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen here is slang for a flamboyant gay man, not the monarch the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes an exaggerated, theatrical manner, which is what acting the queen in the slang sense amounts to.

clue.text: Warning: a large member on cartoonist

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the last

parts.note: taken as written
an arm is a limb, a member of the body
Steve Bell is a political cartoonist for The Guardian

explanation.surface: A smutty tip-off about a well-endowed caricaturist.
explanation.walkthrough: Large member points at innuendo; the member is merely a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm bell is a signal of danger, so figuratively it is any warning sign.

clue.text: Less ruddy tongue action over Brenda!

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a cat laps milk with its tongue
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, giving the royal cipher

explanation.surface: Something rude involving the Queen's tongue leaves her less flushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy means having a reddish, healthy colour, so something paler has less colour in it.

clue.text: He didn't follow Clinton advice initially: "head from Lewinsky bloody hard stuff"

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word advice

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from Lewinsky

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used
gore is blood that has clotted and hardened

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid line about Clinton, Monica Lewinsky and a nasty piece of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Clinton's vice-president lost the 2000 election, so he did not follow Clinton into the White House; head and hard stuff play on the scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Gore was the Democratic successor-in-waiting who lost to Bush, so he never succeeded Clinton as President.

clue.text: Not even rubbish will do for whackos

parts.note: an odd number is one that is not even
balls is British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Even garbage is good enough for crackpots.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for eccentric people whose behaviour seems strange or crazy.

clue.text: Coupling of politicians designed to get the voters interested?

definitions.meaning: suggests a sexual pairing, but means a pair of candidates running together

definitions.text: designed to get the voters interested?
definitions.meaning: a joint slate built to excite the electorate as the perfect combination

explanation.walkthrough: The ticket is a US term for the pair of candidates a party fields together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an ideal pairing of election candidates expected to attract the widest support.

clue.text: Say, a drug-induced session gets end of the bollocks

parts.note: to utter something is to say it
a trip is a spell of hallucination brought on by LSD and the like

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word the

parts.note: the word whose last letter is used

explanation.surface: A druggy evening ends up producing pure nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Bollocks is British slang for nonsense; tripe means rubbish as well as offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are coarse British ways of dismissing something as complete rubbish.

clue.text: State of old queen clinging on to youth (name suppressed)

indicators.note: the queen holds on to what follows, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Mary I and Mary II were queens of England

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is pushed down inside the youth, kept out of view

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: An ageing queen holding on to a young man whose identity has been kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Old queen may suggest an elderly gay man, and the bracketed aside looks like a court reporting restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: Maryland is one of the fifty United States, on the east coast around Chesapeake Bay.

clue.text: Like the web user's agent grabbing unconscious Brenda

indicators.note: the agent grabs the other pieces and holds them inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
the id is the unconscious part of the mind in Freud's theory
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, so it gives the royal cipher

explanation.surface: An internet user's spy seizes a Queen who has passed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Web user sounds like someone online, but the creature using a web is a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: Spidery means resembling a spider, the creature that spins and lives on a web.

clue.text: Bloke as broad as Dr Silver, the powerful board member

parts.note: Dr is the usual short form of doctor, taken here just as printed
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the queen is the most powerful piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A man as wide as a doctor named Silver, the mighty company director.
explanation.walkthrough: Broad is US slang for a woman, so a bloke as a broad is a man dressed as one; board member sounds like a director.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag queen is a man who performs dressed in exaggeratedly feminine clothing.

clue.text: Cyclops is a fruity thing making charge

parts.note: the setter Cyclops speaks of himself as I, so Cyclops is becomes I'm
a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be something juicy that sets off an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often stands for I or ME; here his pseudonym plus is gives I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach a public official is to bring a formal accusation of misconduct against them.

clue.text: Our Brian's despised erection …

definitions.meaning: Private Eye's nickname for Prince Charles
a building he scorned, not anything rude

explanation.walkthrough: In 1984 Prince Charles called a proposed National Gallery extension a monstrous carbuncle on the face of a much-loved friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Since that speech the word for a boil has been the standard insult for an ugly modern building.

clue.text: House of Windsor? Extremely dirty and obnoxious!

indicators.note: taking only the extremes of dirty, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are used
nasty and obnoxious both mean thoroughly unpleasant

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at the royal family as filthy and horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the House of Windsor is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling family whose members succeed one another, like Britain's royal house, is a dynasty.

clue.text: … straight up, without Camilla's lead — that should stop the quarrelling

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so true goes round the letter

parts.note: straight up is slang for honestly, true

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: Continuing the royal theme, honesty from Charles about Camilla might end the rows.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside, not lacking, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement to stop fighting, so it ends a quarrel.

clue.text: President, once fat, pathetic lover

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a former US President
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A former head of state, once overweight, now a sad case in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Abelard, the medieval scholar, loved his pupil Héloïse and was castrated by her family, a famously sad love story.
explanation.definitionFit: Abelard's tragic affair with Héloïse makes him one of history's most pitiable romantic figures.

clue.text: A heavy rub ordered to get sire aroused

indicators.note: the letters of rub are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters rearranged

indicators.note: the letters of sire are stirred up

parts.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A vigorous massage is prescribed to excite a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavy is a noun here, slang for a thug, not the adjective the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruiser is a big, tough man hired for intimidation, the same as a heavy.

clue.text: See 11
Getting right one in Intelligence, a potential nightmare for Bush?

indicators.note: right and one are put in the middle of the intelligence measure

parts.note: IQ is the intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: Getting the intelligence right is a worry for the President, a dig at the WMD dossiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2003 war was justified by faulty intelligence on weapons, which the surface jokes about.
explanation.definitionFit: The invasion and occupation of the Middle Eastern country turned into a long and costly problem for George W Bush.

clue.text: Learn tossing of the organ

indicators.note: tossing the letters of learn throws them into a new order

parts.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Study the art of playing the organ, with a smutty hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ is the kidney, not a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the adjective for things relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Private Eye covers "Bishop left in debt" to be seen everywhere

indicators.note: the magazine's word wraps round the rest like a cover

parts.note: the magazine speaking of itself, so it is us

indicators.note: the departure goes in the middle of the debt note

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt
to quit is to leave, so left gives quit

explanation.surface: The magazine runs a cover story about a cleric who walked out owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: Here left is a verb of leaving, not the political side or the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ubiquitous is present everywhere at once, so you cannot avoid seeing it.

clue.text: The Real IRA, lacking guts, drops one of them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the phrase then drops the letter for one
the phrase loses its middle word, the gut of the three

parts.note: the name whose first word, its gut in the full phrase, is removed
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A dissident Irish republican group, weakened, loses one of its members.
explanation.walkthrough: The Real IRA was a dissident republican group in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive meaning belonging to them, so of them in a sense of ownership.

clue.text: Without thought gives joint to Charlie

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is a jerk

explanation.surface: Something thoughtless passes a joint, or a reefer, to a fool called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is also slang for cocaine, and joint for a cannabis cigarette, which the drug-flavoured surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-jerk reaction is automatic and unthinking, like the reflex when a doctor taps your knee.

clue.text: See 1
See 13
As a course might be rapidly executed in US prison?

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
fried is US slang for executed in the electric chair

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner is quickly put to death in an American jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Course means a dish in a meal, not a programme of study; rapidly hints at quick cooking in a wok.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of a meal may be cooked fast over high heat in a wok while being stirred.
